text:
ConocoPhillips stock ticked up slightly today despite a broader two-week decline, as oil prices held relatively steady with U.S. crude near $82 a barrel. The small gain comes after the stock fell sharply on November 23rd (down to $132.19), suggesting some stabilization, though the collapse of fossil-fuel language at the U.N. climate summit (COP31) over the weekend signals ongoing headwinds for oil-focused companies and their investors.

The stock remains down 2% over two weeks, reflecting the tension energy companies face: while developing economies in Latin America are signaling they'll continue needing oil and gas to fund infrastructure and development, the global climate negotiation process is moving away from explicitly endorsing fossil fuels, creating uncertainty about long-term demand and policy support.
